acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Flame Elementals family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Blaze Warden, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Jet-Gate Specialist (Specialist) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: White-hot central flame with blue edges, two arms shaped into directed jets, and a strong heat-shimmer aura.
Signature mechanic: Twin Jet Gate: one arm becomes a sweeping jet while the other compacts into a bright guard; the roles reverse after each sweep.
battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a lane controller that reshapes both arms into alternating directed jets.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T3 have no obsidian shell, no molten rock, no star, no corona, and no crown; T4 alone gains source-supported obsidian shell and molten rock; T5 alone gains its star, corona, and crown.
Compressed mineral cages, sediment baffles, load-bearing crystal braces, localized dust drops, and pale faults constrain flame motion without converting early forms into rock bodies.
counterplay: Enter behind the sweeping nozzle and strike the exposed core edge before the two arms reverse. Affinity signal: Tier-safe anchors: T1–T3 have no obsidian shell, no molten rock, no star, no corona, and no crown, so one mineral brace fractures after a grounded burst; T4 obsidian shell and molten rock expose a load fault; T5 star, corona, and crown pull against one cracked anchor.
forbiddenTreatments: Rock mass that hides native combustion
identityInvariants: A roughly humanoid upper silhouette dissolves into flame above and tapers or hovers below with no feet.
Temperature remains legible from dull orange through yellow-white to blue-white edges.
Open flame, ember, smoke, and later source-supported obsidian and molten rock stay materially distinct.
Core definition and directed combustion progress from a flicker to a sovereign star while heat remains readable rather than overexposed.
telegraph: One arm narrows to a blue-edged nozzle while the white-hot core leans toward the opposite arm.
